metadata.sourceExcerpt: *Source: OSP Inertia — Identity Fragility Law. Derived from R23, empirically confirmed.* Statement: Semantic identity (two artifacts identical in all shared vocabulary) requires only one vocabulary retraction or divergent addition to break. Identity is a moment, not a stable attractor. It is achieved when all vocabulary is shared and nothing is exclusive; it is broken by any single vocabulary change that introduces exclusivity. Enforcement implication: Identical semantics is not a reliable property to maintain without active governance. Any independent vocabulary change in either artifact breaks identity. Governance mechanisms that require identity must either be point-in-time assertions or must govern all vocabulary changes to both artifacts. Violation detection: SP-10 has no independent violation form — it is a physics fact about the minimum cost to break identity. If an operation is claimed to have preserved identity while introducing an exclusive entry in either artifact, the claim is incorrect and the diff record contains an error. Violations surface as incorrect identity assertions rather than as SP-10 violations directly. Relationship to governance layer: Grounds O-27 (Parasitic Binding) and O-21 (APD) — identity fragility is why detectability (APD element 1) must be actively maintained; the semantic state of an artifact can change by one operation. Also grounds C-18 (Justificatory Computation Verification) — because identity is fragile, the justificatory record of each operation must be produced at operation time, not reconstructed later. ---

metadata.sourceExcerpt: The choice made: The Governed Semantic Kernel (O-17) is architecturally instantiated as five named layers: MCIR (decidable semantic root — "semantic genome"), MCIR-Law (admissibility court), PEIR (regulated expression layer), Domain Effects (immune membrane / effect boundary), ReceiptLog (structural memory). These five layers are the selected C instantiation of the GSK's S-layer containment requirement. S/C split (required): The containment requirement is Specification-layer physics: any valid GSK must contain Turing-complete execution within APD constraints (O-21) through architectural separation. This requirement cannot be configured away — a GSK that does not achieve APD-compliant containment is not a valid GSK. The five-layer Jnana architecture is the selected C instantiation of that requirement. Alternative containment architectures are admissible in principle — a three-layer or seven-layer architecture that achieved the same APD compliance would also satisfy the S-layer requirement — but no such alternatives are currently specified or validated. This selection binds the five-layer Jnana architecture as the operative instantiation until a validated alternative is produced. Each layer maps to a specific invariant or construct enforcement obligation. metadata.sourceExcerpt: Definition: The set of independent code paths through which an invariant must be satisfied in any conforming implementation. Denoted *R(I)* for invariant *I*. A simple invariant ("the function returns an integer") has a small realization surface — every code path that returns from the function must return an integer. A complex invariant ("every governed state mutation produces a receipt before commit") has a large realization surface — every code path that mutates governed state, across every component, must satisfy this invariant; this includes direct mutation paths, paths through helpers, paths through middleware, error-handler unwinding paths, shutdown sequences, retry loops, and so on. The realization surface is a structural property of the invariant relative to the system's component count, interaction depth, and interface multiplicity. It expands faster than prose specification can describe it above the complexity threshold (O-41). Domain: Specification / Realization Depends on: O-02 (Constraint), O-04 (Admissibility Gate), O-09 (CBI) Primary source: Admissibility_Engineering.md (forthcoming) Invariant relationships: Subject of CG-04: realization paths within the surface must each pass admissibility evaluation Grounds CG-08 (Governed Evidence Source Preference): when the realization surface includes paths that produce receipts and paths that do not, evidence preference falls on the receipted paths Razor classification: Refinement of structural-coherence concept already implicit in the SCI Litmus Test ("what CAN exist") at the realization scale. Non-guarantee: The realization surface for a given invariant is not a closed-form quantity. It is system-dependent, architecture-dependent, and grows with system complexity. The construct does not specify a method for exhaustive enumeration; exhaustive enumeration is in general intractable above modest complexity. Contrast: Realization surface ≠ test surface. The test surface is the set of realization paths the test author thought to write tests for. Above the complexity threshold, the realization surface routinely exceeds the test surface; the gap is exactly what plausible-but-wrong realizations (O-40) exploit. ---

Treating plausible-but-wrong as success means accepting structurally invalid output as valid, which violates CG-04 (Admissibility Precedes Effect) at the realization scale. Detection: A specification regime that achieves convergence (O-44) across independent realizations is implicitly closing its saturation gaps. A regime that does not converge — where independent realizations of the same specification produce divergent behaviors — is admitting plausible-but-wrong as success. Tolerable ambiguity is the deliberate preservation of agent discretion within explicitly declared scope; plausible-but-wrong is unintended divergence outside explicit scope. metadata.sourceExcerpt: *Source: CMB-SUBSTRATE-INV Family H, invariants H-1 and H-2. Locked 2026-03-13. Substrate-physics — holds independently of governance.* Statement: Once appended to a substrate event stream, an event record is permanently immutable — its identity, stream membership, prior-chain pointer, and payload do not change. The prior-chain is structurally sound: every non-initial event points to a record that exists in the same stream. No substrate operation removes or modifies existing event records. The history of a semantic artifact's lifecycle is append-only and non-rewritable. Enforcement implication: No governance decision, once receipted in the substrate, can be removed, modified, or retroactively denied. The record of what was decided and when is permanent. Violation detection: If any operation produces an event record whose prior-chain pointer references a non-existent record in the same stream, SP-20 is violated (chain integrity). If any operation modifies an already-appended event record's fields, SP-20 is violated (immutability). Both are detectable by chain traversal on the substrate state. Relationship to governance layer: Grounds CG-02 (Cannot Proceed Silently) — receipts are durable because the substrate that holds them is append-only; SP-20 is the physics that makes "cannot proceed silently" a permanent constraint rather than a revocable one. Grounds O-14 (MCIR) — the three-layer representational structure includes a "separate receipt lineage graph" (PCM-ASTDAG-01) precisely because SP-20 guarantees that once written, receipt lineage is stable and non-rewritable. Non-guarantee: SP-20 does not constrain the payload content of events — H-4 (payload opacity, subsumed by SP-22 in the RC) means no substrate invariant depends on payload semantics. Governance layers may interpret payloads; the substrate holds them as opaque bytes. ---

SP-21 (Reference Graph Monotonicity) — receipted causal chains preserve graph structure across time; in-memory state does not. Razor classification: Refinement of CG-04 at evidence-substrate level. metadata.sourceExcerpt: Intent: Ensure that every analytical act that produces an effect — a receipt, an admission, an integration, a conclusion — is preceded by an explicit authority declaration. Effect without declared authority is an CG-05 violation. Grounding: CG-05 (Authority Must Be Declared) and CG-04 (Admissibility Precedes Effect) — authority must be declared before it is exercised; admissibility must be evaluated before effect is produced. P-3 is the combined operational form of these two invariants. Structure: 1. Before any analytical act that produces a downstream effect, ask: "Under what declared authority am I doing this?" 2. Name the authority explicitly: which invariant, which selection, which declared constraint governs this act? 3. If the authority cannot be named, the act may not proceed. This is not a DEFER — it is a missing mandatory input. Emit REFUSE citing CG-05. 4. Record the authority in the act's receipt. The receipt is not complete without the authority citation. 5. When authority changes between acts (e.g., a new constraint is applied), declare the change explicitly. Do not allow authority to shift silently between steps. Applied in: C-02 (authority binding is mandatory input), C-08 (A-dimension is mandatory; empty A halts crystallization), C-09 (APD checks that authority is visible to agents), C-13 (oracle surfaces force authority into declaration), C-14 (MCIR semantic root must have declared authority), C-16 (S/C/I assignment governs what authority each layer level carries), C-18 (justificatory regime = authority intrinsic to execution). Anti-patterns: *Ambient authority:* proceeding under "it's obvious who has authority here" without declaring it. Obvious authority is not declared authority. CG-05 violation. *Authority by confidence:* treating high confidence in a claim as implying authority to act on it (CC-04: confidence ≠ jurisdiction). High confidence does not declare authority. *Inherited authority:* assuming that because a prior step had declared authority, the current step inherits it without re-declaration. Authority must be declared at each step that exercises it. Prior authority does not flow forward silently. ---

RPZ2.intension: Intent: Ensure that every analytical act that produces an effect — a receipt, an admission, an integration, a conclusion — is preceded by an explicit authority declaration. Effect without declared authority is an CG-05 violation.

metadata.sourceExcerpt: Definition: The structured representation of what did NOT execute in a governed workflow, produced as a required artifact of every execution — not inferred from the absence of log entries. When a gate denies at condition k in a sequential-short-circuit evaluation, conditions k+1 through n are Not-Reached — and the execution record explicitly names each of them as not-reached rather than silently omitting them. When a gate routes via the on_deny branch, the invoke node is Not-Reached — and the execution path record names it as such. A governed execution that omits Not-Reached State for any blocked condition, node, or branch is structurally incomplete, not partially compliant. Three forms of Not-Reached State in a governed execution: 1. Condition not-reached — a condition was not evaluated because a prior condition failed (short-circuit evaluation) 2. Node not-reached — a workflow node (e.g., invoke node) was not executed because the gate routed away from it via the deny branch 3. Branch blocked — an outgoing branch from a gate node was not taken; the alternative branch was taken instead Not-Reached State is the execution-level expression of CG-01 (Negative Certainty): it is the positive record of where continuation stopped and what was explicitly blocked, not merely the absence of evidence that continuation occurred. The difference is structural: absence from a log is uninterpretable without context; a Not-Reached record is a positive governance artifact asserting "this path was blocked by this gate decision, under this specification." Domain: Governance / Execution Semantics Depends on: O-05 (Refusal), O-07 (Negative Certainty), O-33 (Declared Admissibility Specification) Primary source(s): - CMB-PAPER §§2–4 (not-reached state semantics; FLOW-2 execution path rendering; short-circuit condition recording; not-reached as first-class path, not log absence) - CMB-EXTERN §3 (receipted denial; [ -- ] notation as positive not-reached record; structured denial outcome) - CMB-PAPER abstract ("execution trace including not-reached nodes" as unified artifact of every execution) - Source type note: CMB sources describe implemented behavior. Not-Reached State is operational

metadata.sourceExcerpt: *Reclassified from INV-01. Constitutional governance invariant.* Statement: Knowledge of where continuation must stop is itself a form of knowledge. A system in the Ableman framework can assert that inference, escalation, or action cannot legitimately proceed from a given state — and this assertion is epistemically valid without requiring positive claims about what is true. Negative certainty bounds without accumulating. It is terminal under fixed authority — it does not open new inference paths or license downstream claims. Enforcement implication: Every governed system must be capable of producing stopping-condition outputs as first-class positive artifacts. A system that cannot emit REFUSE or UNDECIDABLE receipts is constitutionally non-compliant. Refusal is not failure; it is the exercise of a governance capacity. Violation detection: Violated when a governed system emits no REFUSE or UNDECIDABLE outputs across a corpus of evaluations, or when stopping conditions are recorded as absences rather than positive receipted artifacts. Silent non-continuation (no receipt for a stopping condition) is a CG-01 violation detectable by receipt chain audit. Physics grounding: SP-11 (Anti-Convergence) — negative certainty exists as a first-class output precisely because there is no natural resolution to fall back on; when evaluation reaches a structural boundary, the correct output is the boundary itself, not a forced admission. SP-05 (Pattern Monotonicity Under Removal) — the one-way nature of removal means some boundaries are permanent; negative certainty is the epistemic expression of permanent structural boundaries. SP-04 (Divergence Under Parallel Expansion) — under fixed authority, the divergence gradient means structural boundaries do not self-resolve; negative certainty is terminal precisely because the physics offers no path back toward admission under fixed authority. Enforcement mechanism: C-03 (Refusal Construction) and C-04 (Negative Certainty Declaration). GateHalt hierarchy and RefusalReceipt in OSP phases/phase2.py. Receipt chain audit via validation/chain.py. ---

The reviewer's framing: "this tension is not a flaw. It is probably unavoidable. But it is the deepest philosophical pressure point in the system. Because the codex is trying to constitutionalize something that is inherently partially fluid." The frontier: The corpus currently holds determinism and emergence in productive tension *implicitly*. Neither side is abandoned. But no construct or invariant *names* the tension as a meta-relationship. The framework may eventually benefit from making the tension explicit — not as a Razor Expansion (no new degree of freedom would be introduced; both sides are already in the corpus) but as a Refinement clarifying that determinism and emergence are co-constitutive rather than opposing. Specifically: Determinism applies at the substrate layer (SP-18, SP-19) and the governance gate (CG-04). It is what makes auditable governance possible. Emergence applies at the field layer (SP-11 through SP-16) and the lexical layer (O-62). It is what makes the substrate worth governing — a fully deterministic field would have no semantic content to govern. metadata.sourceExcerpt: The choice made: The Ableman Format Specification (AFS, O-52) instantiates in two architecturally complementary forms — the document-type instantiation (CX:AES, O-20) and the database-type instantiation (CMB, O-12) — as peer architectures sharing substrate properties. They are not collapsed into a single instantiation with content-type tagging, nor are they fragmented into three or more instantiation classes. Rationale: Semantic content has two operational modes. Document character (composed once, refined as a unified whole, consumed end-to-end) is structurally distinct from database character (accreted incrementally, queried by partial match, evolved entry by entry). Forcing all semantic content into one instantiation produces friction: a 10,000-entry domain dictionary expressed as a Codex is unreadable; a small system specification expressed as a database loses the document-level coherence Codices provide. AFS supports both because semantic content has both modes, and the same governance discipline must apply to both. The two instantiations are *peers*, not levels of a hierarchy. Both inherit AFS substrate properties (per CG-09): receipted transitions, admissibility gating, refusal as first-class, content-addressed identity, lineage preservation. The instantiations differ in operational mode, not in governance strictness. Three instantiation classes (or more) would require evidence that semantic content has a third operational mode beyond document and database character. No such evidence currently exists. A single instantiation with content-type tagging would collapse the document/ database distinction into a runtime flag, losing the architectural separation that motivates the two-instantiation design. Alternatives considered: - Single instantiation with content-type tagging (rejected — collapses operational distinction) - Three or more instantiations (rejected — no current evidence of a third operational mode) - Hierarchical instantiation (CX as primary, CMB as derivative) (rejected — collapses the peering) Source: Constitutional_Crystallized_Meaning_Base.md (forthcoming) §1; AFS umbrella paper [forthcoming] §2. Cross-paper signal: Strong — multiple new corpu

metadata.sourceExcerpt: *Source: OSP Semantic Change Law 1. Derived from R20/R21, empirically confirmed.* Statement: If two semantic artifacts have no shared vocabulary (payload separation), additive refinement of either artifact does not produce shared vocabulary unless a new entry explicitly intersects the other artifact's existing vocabulary. Semantic separation is stable under additive refinement that avoids the other artifact's conceptual space. Enforcement implication: Basin topology (O-30) is not an artifact of insufficient vocabulary — it reflects genuine conceptual distance. An analyst who finds two artifacts in separate basins cannot dissolve the separation through refinement alone; they must make a deliberate vocabulary decision. Violation detection: If two artifacts transition from payload separation to overlap without any vocabulary entry explicitly intersecting the other's labels, SP-01 is violated. This is detectable by comparing diff outputs before and after refinement. Relationship to governance layer: Grounds CG-04 (Admissibility Precedes Effect) and CG-06 (Governance Operates on Structure) — structural separation is stable and detectable, which is why structural evaluation (not interpretive judgment) can serve as the basis for admissibility decisions. ---

metadata.sourceExcerpt: *Source: Constitutional_Semantic_Crystallization (consolidated, forthcoming) §7.4. Substrate-physics invariant; refines SP-20 in the crystallization context.* Statement: A binding artifact modified after crossing the Constitutional Semantic Crystallization (CSC, O-55) boundary, without producing a new crystallization receipt, loses lineage. The artifact's content-addressed identity (SP-18) may persist if its canonical form is unchanged, but its semantic state may have shifted; the receipt log fails to record the change. This is structurally indistinguishable from substrate fault and must be treated as such. Enforcement implication: Every modification to a constitutionally bound artifact must produce a new crystallization receipt before the modification takes effect. Modifications without crystallization receipts are inadmissible. Detection requires audit of the receipt chain at every binding-artifact mutation boundary. Violation detection: Violated when (a) a binding artifact's canonical form changes between two epochs, AND (b) no crystallization receipt records the change between those epochs. Detection: chain audit + canonical-form comparison. Physics grounding: SP-20 (Event Immutability and Prior Chain Integrity) — the append-only property of the lineage chain is the substrate physics that makes lineage preservation possible. SP-24 sharpens SP-20 at the crystallization-boundary scale: not only must the chain be append-only, but every binding-state change must be appended to the chain or the change has not occurred in a governance- relevant sense. Enforcement mechanism: Crystallization receipts at every CMB mutation boundary; gate-predicate evaluation receipted at boundary crossings; receipt chain audit identifies hash-stable artifacts whose canonical form has shifted without recorded crystallization event. ---

metadata.sourceExcerpt: *Source: OSP Field Effect — Density Amplification. Derived from R28, empirically confirmed.* Statement: A semantic artifact entering a high-density population receives more total shared vocabulary per vocabulary entry added than the same artifact in a sparse population. Field density amplifies the return on vocabulary investment. Enforcement implication: Semantic mass (O-24 SGC) accumulates non-linearly — the same governance actions produce greater shared- structure yield in a dense field than in a sparse one. SGC is a threshold phenomenon: early governance produces little shared structure; governance in a mature field produces compounding returns. Violation detection: SP-14 is a field-level statistical law. If a corpus analysis claims vocabulary additions in a high-density field produce no greater shared structure than in a sparse field (controlling for artifact count), SP-14 is contradicted. This requires evidence that the density measurement or population selection is incorrect. Non-guarantee: SP-14 describes a statistical tendency over populations; it does not guarantee that any specific vocabulary addition will produce shared structure in a high-density field. A vocabulary entry can be added to an artifact that shares no vocabulary with any neighbor, regardless of field density. Relationship to governance layer: Grounds O-24 (SGC) directly — the field condition assessment (C-20) is qualitative precisely because SP-14 describes a tendency, not a deterministic output. Also grounds O-30 (Semantic Basin) — basin formation accelerates in high-density regions because SP-14 makes vocabulary decisions in those regions more productive. ---

RPZ2.intension: A semantic artifact entering a high-density population receives more total shared vocabulary per vocabulary entry added than the same artifact in a sparse population. Field density amplifies the return on vocabulary investment.

metadata.sourceExcerpt: *Source: CMB-SUBSTRATE-INV Family V, invariant V-3 (Context Isolation). Locked 2026-03-13. Substrate-physics — holds independently of governance.* Statement: Artifact resolution is scoped to a declared resolution context. A result of "not found" from a resolution operation means the artifact is absent from this context — not globally absent. Multiple resolution contexts may coexist, each providing a different view of what artifacts exist. Resolution is deterministic within a context but does not assert facts about other contexts. Enforcement implication: An analyst who finds that an artifact does not resolve in one context cannot conclude the artifact does not exist globally. The correct conclusion is scoped: "absent from this context." This bounds inference — a "not found" result is negative certainty within a declared scope, not a global ontological claim. Violation detection: If a system concludes "artifact does not exist" (globally) from a "not found" in a single resolution context, SP-23 is violated at the inference level. Detection: audit analytical conclusions for unscoped absence claims — any claim of the form "X does not exist" that does not name the resolution context in which it was tested. Relationship to governance layer: Grounds O-31 (Constitutional Compatibility) directly — compatibility evaluation must be context- scoped; a compatibility claim must name the resolution context in which it holds. A compatibility verdict produced from a single unscoped resolution is not an admissible compatibility claim under SP-23. Grounds O-07 (Negative Certainty) — V-3 provides the substrate-level physics that makes context-scoped certainty a valid and well-defined output; "not found in this context" is not ignorance, it is scoped negative certainty with a deterministic basis. Non-guarantee: SP-23 does not define how multiple resolution contexts relate to each other, or how cross-context resolution is performed. Those are Configuration matters (CC-*), not substrate physics. --- ## Part II — Constitutional Governance Invariants (CG-*) ---

metadata.sourceExcerpt: The choice made: The Admissibility Gate (O-04) emits DEFER under exactly two conditions: (a) Insufficient evidence — the evidence required to evaluate the declared admissibility constraints is not yet present, but is expected to become available; (b) Oracle input required — evaluation depends on an undeclared oracle surface (O-26) that must be declared and consulted before the gate can reach a terminal state. DEFER carries an implicit expectation of resolution: it is not an indefinite suspension but a bounded pause. A DEFER that does not resolve to ADMIT or REFUSE within a deployment-declared time bound escalates to REFUSE. REFUSE is the correct output when: integrity conditions fail (a constraint is violated), authority is absent or undeclarable (CG-05 cannot be satisfied), or the oracle surface cannot be declared or consulted (the dependency is ungovernable). REFUSE is not DEFER — REFUSE is terminal; DEFER is suspended. Rationale: The CX-S layer (CG-04, O-04) declares DEFER as a legitimate gate state but does not specify the threshold between DEFER and REFUSE. This is a deployment decision: different governance contexts have different tolerances for suspended evaluation. The EIR formulation (PCM-EIR-06) provides the correct trigger vocabulary (insufficient evidence / oracle input required) and this selection adopts it as binding. The time-bound escalation rule is required by CG-04 — a DEFER that never resolves allows effects to accumulate while evaluation is perpetually suspended, which violates the spirit of admissibility-precedes-effect even if each individual step technically produces a DEFER receipt. Alternatives considered: - DEFER for any uncertainty (broad threshold): rejected — collapses the DEFER/REFUSE distinction; a gate that DEFERs whenever uncertain never terminates, producing the same structural problem as a gate that does not exist. - No DEFER state (binary ADMIT/REFUSE only): rejected — removes the legitimate suspended-evaluation case, forcing REFUSE when the correct epistemic response is "not yet determinable." metadata.sourceExcerpt: Definition: The set of loci in a semantic system where legitimacy or inference depends on undeclared authority or interpretation external to the formal structure of that system. In a governed semantic system under MCIR (O-14), MCIR forces every oracle surface to be either explicitly declared or to produce a refusal — implicit oracle surfaces are not admissible in a governed semantic system. An oracle surface is the structural target of CG-05: the location in a system where authority declaration is required before the authority can be exercised. metadata.sourceExcerpt: Domain: Corpus governance / ontology hygiene Selection (Configuration layer; admitted v1.9): The framework selects an *explicit retirement protocol* for ontology elements (constructs, invariants, selections, components, patterns) rather than monotonic-growth-only admission discipline. Construct admission and construct retirement are co-required operations of a healthy semantic system per SP-25 (Productive Tension). CC-11 specifies the procedural mechanism for retirement; SP-25 grounds the necessity substrate-physically. Procedural mechanism: 1. Demotion criteria. A PROVISIONAL construct that has not earned promotion to ADMISSIBLE within a defined window (recommended: two ARC version cycles) becomes a *retirement candidate*. The candidacy is evaluated against: - Cross-paper validation status (any new primary source admitting the construct independently?) - Working-deployment evidence (has the construct been load-bearing in a real deployment?) - SCI Litmus Test re-application (does removing this construct change what the framework can express, or only how things are described?) - Downstream load (do other constructs depend on this construct, and would those dependents fail without it?) 2. Supersession criteria. A construct is superseded when another construct's content fully captures its operational role. Supersession collapses N constructs into 1 (the absorbing construct gains the absorbed content as sub-structure). Distinct from fusion (CC-12), which is N-into-1 merge with both contributing. 3. Merge criteria (consolidation pathway). A construct is consolidated when its content is absorbed into an existing construct as sub-structure. Used in v1.9 for O-42 → O-39, O-62 → O-57, O-63 → O-57, CG-12 → O-57. The retired construct is replaced by a *tombstone redirect* preserving its slot identifier with a resolution pointer to the absorbing construct. 4. Archival lineage preservation. Retired constructs are not deleted from ONTOLOGY.md / INVARIANTS.md; they remain as tombstone redirects with retirement rationale. metadata.sourceExcerpt: Origin: v1.9.4 patch (2026-05-06) following inspection of the gtk_chess_resolver reference archive and review of the synthesis framing that placed semantic governance primitives in operating- system-primitive correspondence (binding integrity ↔ memory protection; semantic scope isolation ↔ process isolation; authority scopes ↔ permissions; GTK identity bindings ↔ symbol tables; receipt chains ↔ filesystem lineage; etc.). Observation: The gtk_chess_resolver archive exhibits substrate- level primitives (kernel.py, cir.py, authority.py, cmb_substrate.py, receipts.py, acts.py, audits.py) operating across two domains (chess and Python) under a shared substrate. The runtime architecture suggests that semantic systems above a threshold complexity may require typed runtime primitives organized in identifiable categories. The synthesis framing that surfaced this observation proposed an extensive correspondence with operating-system primitives. The hypothesis (testable claim): Semantic systems exercising governed runtime continuity exhibit primitive categories that recur across deployments in identifiable classes — at minimum: binding integrity, semantic scope isolation, authority scope, receipt lineage, namespace control, admissibility gating, and refusal-as- first-class. If true, the recurrence is *structural* (caused by the operational pressures of governed semantic systems at scale), not analogical (pattern-matched onto deployments by reasoning). The narrower form of this claim — and the one this OQ tracks — is: the categories will recur in additional substrate deployments beyond the two domains (chess, Python) currently exercised in the reference archive. A third domain (legal, scientific terminology, robotics command, medical, multi-agent coordination, or institutional ontology) will surface the same primitive classes without requiring new primitive categories specific to that domain. The null hypothesis: Substrate primitives in deployed semantic systems are domain-shaped, not class-shaped. Each new domain introduces primitives specific to its operational pressures; the primitives in the reference archive are the chess+Python intersection, not a substrate-level nece

metadata.sourceExcerpt: Definition: The epistemic state in which a system has determined that continuation cannot legitimately proceed from a given state under declared constraints. Negative certainty is a structured, positive output — it carries the knowledge of where the boundary is, without making claims about what lies beyond it. It is not the absence of knowledge; it is a specific kind of knowledge: a bound on legitimate continuation. Terminal under fixed authority (SMT formulation): Negative certainty is "terminal under fixed authority — not resolved by waiting or computation" (SMT §4 Undecidability, PCM-SMT-04). Where CBI §5 defined negative certainty as knowledge of where continuation is impossible, SMT adds the temporal dimension: it is not a temporary epistemic gap but a structural terminus under the declared authority regime. Asymmetric (CBI formulation): Negative certainty does not accumulate authority or license overreach (CBI §5, PCM-CBI-10). It bounds what may be claimed, inferred, or propagated — it does not expand the space of admissible claims or grant downstream authority. A stopping condition cannot be used to assert positive claims about adjacent territory. Topological expression: Collapse ridges in semantic field topology (O-30 Semantic Basin, SFA framework, PCM-SFA-02) are the topological form of O-07 at field scale — the boundaries where admissible reasoning paths terminate. O-07 is the pointwise property; collapse ridges are the field-level structure through which that property is expressed. Cross-reference note (dual appearance): Negative Certainty appears as both CG-01 and O-07. This is intentional and must be understood precisely. CG-01 states that stopping conditions must be treated as outputs; O-07 names the epistemic state that results when they are. The invariant is the structural requirement; the construct is the epistemic state that satisfies it. A system that correctly applies CG-01 produces O-07 states. A system that reaches an O-07 state without receipting it violates CG-02. Domain: Epistemics Depends on: O-05 (Refusal) Primary source: Admissible_Epistemology.md §8; Constraint-Bound_Inference_Math_Paper.md Invariant relationships: Construct instanti

metadata.sourceExcerpt: Definition: The structural boundary enforcing that no semantic artifact becomes operative — influences decisions, grounds inference, or authorizes action — until it has passed admissibility evaluation via the Admissibility Gate (O-04). The Membrane separates the semantic layer (proposal, structure, evaluation) from the execution layer (effect, action, downstream reliance). The Epistemic Membrane is the construct that instantiates CG-04 — it is not the invariant itself but the structural form through which the invariant holds in any governed system. CG-04 states what must hold; the Membrane describes how it holds. Domain: Epistemics Depends on: O-04 (Admissibility Gate) Primary source: Admissible_Epistemology.md §4 Invariant relationships: Structural enforcement of CG-04: the Membrane IS the admissibility-before-effect boundary Instantiates CG-02: the Membrane is where receipts are issued for every crossing (admission or refusal) Relates to CG-06: the Membrane enforces that only structural evaluation — not narrative persuasion — determines what crosses Non-guarantee — Boundary Leakage: The Epistemic Membrane has a named failure mode: Boundary Leakage — the failure mode in which ungoverned meaning contaminates governed semantic state through a gap, absence, or subversion of the Membrane. Boundary Leakage is distinct from Corruption (O-18): Corruption operates inside the governed layer with false receipts; Boundary Leakage bypasses the governed layer entirely, introducing ungoverned material before it can be evaluated. No detection protocol for Boundary Leakage is specified in this Codex version. The failure mode is named and structurally located; detection spec is an open item for the post-ingestion authoring session. Contrast: Epistemic Membrane ≠ security boundary or access control layer. A security boundary governs who may act. The Epistemic Membrane governs what is permitted to count — it is an epistemic boundary, not an authorization boundary. ---

metadata.sourceExcerpt: What it does: Assesses whether a governed execution exhibits a Governance Coverage Gap (O-35) — verifies that all governance layers declared applicable to the operation family (N) actually participated in the execution (k), and that any non-participation is explicitly recorded. Produces a coverage verdict with gap magnitude N−k and form classification (Layer Non-Activation, Layer Absence, or Layer Bypass) when a gap is found. Inputs: - The executed operation and its operation family classification - The declared applicable governance layer set N (from governance declaration or equivalent; N-determination strategy must be stated) - The execution record indicating which layers produced evaluation events for this execution (k) - The non-participation record surface for this execution context (are there durable records of which layers did not participate?) Outputs: Coverage verdict — COVERED (k = N) or GAPPED (k < N). For GAPPED: gap magnitude (N − k), form classification for each non-participating layer (Layer Non-Activation / Layer Absence / Layer Bypass), and a non-participation record assessment (is the gap recorded or unrecorded?). Unrecorded gap is O-35 confirmed. Recorded gap is intentional partial governance (not O-35). Admissibility constraint: C-27 may only produce a GAPPED verdict when N is stated. Where N cannot be determined, the component records "O-35 suspicion — N indeterminate" and halts. See GCG Codex v1.0 for N-determination procedure (DECLARED-N, PER-CONTEXT-N, MINIMUM-N, MAXIMUM-N strategies). Invariants enforced: - CG-02 (Cannot Proceed Silently): non-participating declared governance layers that leave no record are a CG-02 violation at the governance architecture level; C-27 is the detection mechanism - CG-04 (Admissibility Precedes Effect): in a multi-layer model, CG-04 requires all declared applicable layers to evaluate before effects proceed; C-27 verifies this across the N-layer set - CG-05 (Authority Must Be Declared): non-participating layers represent undeclared absence of authority; C-27 surfaces the gap between declared and realized authority participation Full application specification: GCG Codex v1.0 (Constitutional Codex, Conceptua

metadata.sourceExcerpt: ## (O-21 open tension obligation not yet fulfilled by CX-C) Observation: O-21 (Ableman Prime Directive) carries an explicit open tension note: "unconstrained Turing-completeness is structurally incompatible with APD detectability, because arbitrary self-modification makes binding visibility undecidable. TAPD's proposed resolution is architectural separation via the Jnana layers (O-17 cross-reference). This tension is noted but not resolved within the RC — it is a CX-C design obligation." Examining CX-C/CONFIGURATION.md, the five current selections (CC-01 through CC-05) govern property vocabulary, MCIR representational structure, Jnana architecture, DEFER threshold, and Termination Taxonomy. None of them explicitly prohibits Turing-complete operations at the MCIR semantic root. The Jnana architecture (CC-03) describes the five layers and their boundaries but does not specify what computational model is permitted at the MCIR root layer. The O-21 tension is therefore named but unresolved in CX-C. What the missing selection must accomplish: Prohibit Turing-complete operations at the MCIR semantic root layer State this as fulfillment of the O-21 APD detectability requirement Clarify that Turing-complete operations are permitted at higher Jnana layers (PEIR, Domain Effects) — the restriction is specific to the semantic root Add at least two inadmissible directions: one for Turing-complete operations at the root, one for binding visibility implemented as a runtime query requiring full execution Why this is CX-C and not CX-S: The prohibition is a configuration decision about what computational model is used at the MCIR root — it is an architectural choice, not a necessary feature of semantic governance per se. A theoretical framework could in principle operate with a Turing-complete semantic root (at the cost of APD detectability), making this a selection rather than an invariant. Relationship to OQ-01 and OQ-02: This is the most structurally urgent of the three OQs because it closes an explicitly flagged obligation in O-21. OQ-01 and OQ-02 add new constructs; OQ-03 repairs an existing gap in the CX-C layer that leaves APD compliance claims incomplete. Status: RESOLVED

metadata.sourceExcerpt: *Source: OSP Inertia — Dimensional Independence Law. Derived from R23, empirically confirmed.* Statement: Operations in one semantic dimension do not affect distance in another. Adding or removing vocabulary from the D-dimension does not change C-dimension, K-dimension, or A-dimension distance between artifacts. Dimensions are orthogonal under vocabulary change. Enforcement implication: The four MCIR dimensions (D, C, K, A) of O-14 are genuinely independent — coupling between dimensions is not a physics property but a declared governance constraint (K-dimension). This is why K-dimension coupling restrictions are meaningful: they constrain what is otherwise independent. Violation detection: If a vocabulary operation in dimension X produces a measurable change in the diff output of dimension Y (absent a declared K-dimension coupling), SP-07 is violated. Relationship to governance layer: Grounds O-14 (MCIR) — the four-dimension structure is coherent precisely because dimensions are independent. Also grounds CC-01 (Property Vocabulary as Configuration Layer) — vocabulary can be configured per-dimension without cross-dimension interference. ---

metadata.sourceExcerpt: *Source: OSP Field Effect — Field Transmission. Derived from R28, empirically confirmed.* Statement: When an artifact converges toward a member of a dense semantic field, that convergence propagates shared vocabulary to the field's other members automatically. A single convergent vocabulary decision has multiplied consequences in a dense field — the convergent artifact acquires shared vocabulary with all field members whose vocabulary overlaps the target's. Enforcement implication: In a dense field, single governance actions have leverage. Crystallizing one artifact's relationship to a field-embedded artifact creates shared structure with the entire field cluster simultaneously. Governance in dense fields is more powerful — and more risky — than in sparse fields. Violation detection: SP-16 is a field-level statistical law. If convergence toward a high-density field member produces no shared vocabulary increase with other field members (when the target shares vocabulary with those members), SP-16 is contradicted. This indicates either the target is not embedded in the field as claimed or the vocabulary intersection is not as described. Non-guarantee: vocabulary overlap may reflect coincidentally identical labels rather than genuine conceptual relation — two fields independently developing the same term do not thereby share meaning. The field transmission is structural; whether the transmitted shared structure is conceptually coherent is an analytical judgment, not a physics fact. Relationship to governance layer: Grounds O-24 (SGC) and O-17 (GSK) — field transmission is why governance must be positioned at the semantic root rather than at individual artifacts; actions at the root propagate through the field. Also grounds CG-05 (Authority Must Be Declared) — in a dense field, undeclared authority propagates as automatically as declared authority; the amplification of SP-16 applies to ungoverned influence as much as governed influence. ---

metadata.sourceExcerpt: Definition: The theoretical framework in which knowledge is defined by admissibility — the capacity of a semantic artifact to survive explicit constraint evaluation without violating declared invariants. Admissible Epistemology replaces truth-correspondence with permission conditions. It treats refusal as a first-class epistemic output (O-05), assigns cost to meaning via Meaning-Inertia (O-08), and enforces a strict separation between semantic validation and execution via the Epistemic Membrane (O-06). The governing question is not "is this true?" but "is this permitted to count?" Domain: Epistemics Depends on: O-01 (Semantic Artifact), O-02 (Constraint) Primary source: Admissible_Epistemology.md Invariant relationships: Instantiates CG-04: admissibility evaluation precedes all epistemic effect Applies CG-03 at the epistemic level: the framework's explicit limits are a constitutive feature, not a disclaimer The framework whose coherent operation CG-01, CG-02, CG-05, and CG-06 collectively govern Non-guarantee: Admissible Epistemology does not guarantee that admitted artifacts are true in any correspondence sense — only that they have survived declared constraint evaluation. Admissibility ≠ truth. Contrast: Admissible Epistemology ≠ classical epistemology (correspondence, coherence, pragmatic). Classical frameworks ask whether a belief mirrors reality, fits a belief system, or works. Admissible Epistemology asks the prior question: is this permitted to count at all? ---

metadata.sourceExcerpt: The choice made: Property vocabulary — the declared set of evaluable properties per PCM type — is a CX-C configuration decision, not an intrinsic property of semantic artifacts. Each deployment declares its own property vocabulary; that vocabulary is not embedded in the artifact definitions themselves. Rationale: O-15 (Meaning as Binding) is a Specification-layer claim: meaning is constituted by relational binding structure, not by local vocabulary entries. OSP IQ-01 (COMPATIBILITY_PREDICATE_ENGINE) requires locally evaluable properties per PCM type. These operate at different SCI layers. O-15 governs what meaning IS (S — removing it changes what can exist: relational vs. intrinsic meaning). Property vocabulary governs HOW relational predicates are evaluated in a particular deployment (C — removing a specific vocabulary changes how meaning is accessed, not what meaning is). The conflict dissolves when the layers are correctly assigned. This selection makes the assignment binding. Alternatives considered: - Revise O-15 to permit intrinsic vocabulary: rejected — demotes an S-layer claim to C, collapsing the relational/intrinsic distinction O-15 was admitted to name. - Treat property vocabulary as S (declare a universal vocabulary): rejected — would make all deployments share an identical vocabulary, eliminating the configuration dimension that domain-specific applications require. Reconfiguration trigger: Evidence that relational predicate evaluation cannot be performed without a vocabulary that is itself fixed at the Specification layer — i.e., if a universal minimal vocabulary is found to be required by the framework's invariants regardless of deployment context. This would require an O-15 amendment and a corresponding S-layer addition before this selection could change. Blast radius: Any CX-I component implementing COMPATIBILITY_PREDICATE_ENGINE (OSP IQ-01) must treat property vocabulary as a runtime configuration parameter, not a hard-coded constant. Moderate blast radius — contained to the meaning-evaluation pipeline. O-15 unchanged; no CX-S amendments required. metadata.sourceExcerpt: *Source: CMB-SUBSTRATE-INV Family I, invariant I-3. Locked 2026-03-13 (CMB Substrate Invariant Canon, Governor 7ACD). Substrate-physics — holds at the artifact-existence layer independently of governance.* Statement: Two artifacts are substrate-identical if and only if they produce the same hash digest under the same encoding version. An artifact's identity is constituted by a cryptographic hash of its canonical encoding — not by its name, location, or declaration history. The substrate treats hash equality as identity equality. This relies on SHA-256 collision resistance as a stated assumption, not a derivable consequence. Enforcement implication: Canonical identity is content-derived and global. Two artifacts with identical logical content, compiled anywhere, have identical identities. The identity cannot be forged by re-labeling, relocating, or re-declaring an artifact. Violation detection: If any operation in a governed system treats two artifacts with the same hash digest as non-identical (or two artifacts with different digests as identical), SP-18 is violated. Detectable by comparing hash outputs of canonical_encode applied to any two artifact declarations. Relationship to governance layer: Grounds O-14 (MCIR) — the four-dimensional crystallized integrity record is constituted by its hash identity, not by its declared name; SP-18 is the physics that makes MCIR identity non-negotiable. Grounds O-12 (CMB) — the crystallization pipeline produces a canonical MCIR artifact only if artifact identity is content-derived; SP-18 is the physics that makes crystallization produce a stable, verifiable output rather than a mutable claim. Grounds O-31 (Constitutional Compatibility) — compatibility evaluation requires stable identity to be tractable; SP-18 is the physics that makes compatibility a well-defined question. Non-guarantee: SP-18 does not assert that SHA-256 collisions are impossible — it states the substrate assumes collision resistance as a mathematical property. If SHA-256 is broken, SP-18 is not a violated semantic physics law; it is a violated substrate assumption requiring a version migration. ---

Derived from R24, empirically confirmed.* Statement: There is no natural tendency for semantic systems to converge toward identity. Left to independent development, semantic artifacts diverge. Convergence requires deliberate, coordinated vocabulary decisions. The default trajectory of any uncoordinated semantic system is increasing separation. Enforcement implication: Shared semantic structure does not accumulate spontaneously. Every instance of shared vocabulary between independent artifacts is the result of a deliberate decision. metadata.sourceExcerpt: Definition: Corruption ≠ error. Error is unintentional deviation from a correct process — it can be detected and corrected by re-running the process. Corruption is continuation that has passed formal governance checks while violating substantive constraints — it is harder to detect precisely because the receipt chain appears intact, the authority bindings appear valid, and the artifact appears to have been admitted legitimately. Corruption is the failure mode of governance systems that maintain their outward form while their substantive operation has been subverted. More precisely: Corruption is the named failure mode in which a semantic or governance process continues past the point at which it should have halted, producing a receipt chain or authority structure that is formally present but substantively invalid. Corruption is not the absence of governance — it is governance whose receipts lie. Three authority laundering sub-types: Authority laundering (see five-pattern taxonomy below) operates through three named mechanisms: (a) Inference laundering — bypassing admissibility through a reasoning chain without gate crossing; legitimacy derived from inference, not from declaration (CBI §7, PCM-CBI-12: "continuation laundering through inference"); (b) Repetition laundering — legitimacy through repetition, hierarchical embedding, or procedural normalization rather than warrant; authority accretes by momentum (COR §4.4, PCM-COR-03); (c) Proximity laundering — authority transfer via contextual proximity or reuse; an artifact adjacent to a legitimate authority source is treated as inheriting that authority without explicit grant (SLBC §6, PCM-SLBC-03: "contextual proximity transfers authority without warrant"). Five corruption patterns (COR §4, PCM-COR-03): (1) Inertial Continuation — authority persists by momentum without renewal; (2) Exception Creep — temporary deviations normalize without renegotiation; (3) Semantic/Bureaucratic Drift — invariants erode while form is preserved; (4) Authority Laundering — legitimacy through repetition, hierarchy, or procedure rather than warrant (see three sub-types above); (5) Boundary Obscuration — drift or intentional concealment

metadata.sourceExcerpt: *Source: OSP Inertia — Unit Cost Law. Derived from R23, empirically confirmed.* Statement: Every vocabulary addition or removal produces exactly one unit of change in the corresponding semantic dimension. Semantic operations are atomic — no sub-unit operation produces fractional change, and no single operation produces more than one unit in a single dimension. Enforcement implication: Inertia is quantifiable. Because each operation costs exactly one unit, the distance between any two semantic states is an integer count of operations. Violation detection: If a single declared vocabulary operation produces a diff showing more than one new shared or exclusive entry in a single dimension, SP-06 is violated. metadata.sourceExcerpt: Definition: The structural principle that receipts in a governed execution exist in three distinct layers with non-interchangeable roles and a fixed temporal ordering relative to effects. The three layers are: - Decision Layer — produced *before* any effect occurs. Records the governance evaluation outcome (ALLOW, DENY, CONDITIONAL, NO_ENFORCEMENT). The absence of a Decision-layer receipt on an effect means the effect was ungoverned. - Operation Layer — produced *after* a successful operation. Records what happened as a result of a Decision-layer ALLOW. Structurally absent in a DENY path — and that absence is itself informative, not a gap. - Persistence Layer — the append-only storage and retrieval mechanism through which Decision and Operation receipts are recorded and remain auditable after execution completes. The three layers must not be conflated. A Decision receipt produced after the effect it governs is not a Decision receipt — it is an audit fabrication. An Operation receipt produced without a prior Decision ALLOW violates CG-04. Types may not be reused across layers. The temporal ordering is: Decision → (effect if ALLOW) → Operation → Persistence. On DENY: Decision → Persistence (no Operation receipt produced, and its absence confirms the effect did not occur). metadata.sourceExcerpt: Definition: The constitutional lexical primitive — the smallest stable unit of disambiguated semantic identity. A GTK is a typed three-part object: 1. Binding Identity — the resolved semantic point; the specific concept-binding currently invoked (e.g., bank(financial institution) versus bank(river edge)). 2. Alias Set — what other words can call this concept (e.g., sofa ↔ couch; physician ↔ doctor in the medical sense). This component subsumes WordNet-style synsets. 3. Competing Binding Set — what other concepts this surface form can call (e.g., bank → financial institution, river edge, aviation maneuver, memory reserve). Polysemy as topology. GTK length is unconstrained (clarification added v1.9.2): GTK identity is defined by *stability under reference*, not by length or brevity. The "smallest stable unit" qualifier in the definition is structural, not literal: a GTK occupies the position where compression and stability meet — where the binding can be referenced consistently across contexts but where further compression would lose binding identity. Forms that are short but unstable (drift across resolutions) are not GTKs; forms that are long but stable (a multi-part identifier with explicit version, scope, and authority signatures) can be GTKs. What disqualifies a candidate from being a GTK is drift tolerance, not length. A GTK can be: a single word (chess:queen.piece) a phrase (governed-coding:thrash-threshold) a structured object (an equation, a protocol identifier, a doctrine name with explicit signature, a graph fragment) in principle, longer than a sentence if that length is what stable binding identity requires for the concept in question This clarification matters for downstream architectural reasoning: encyclopedia entries decompress *from* the GTK seed; they are not the GTK's "long version." See OQ-19 for the related compression-gradient direction tracked separately. The Competing Binding Set is the canonical site of *polysemy as topology* (consolidated from former O-62 in v1.9): polysemy is not evidence against stable lexical meaning to be resolved as defect; it is the structure of the lexical lattice itself, indexed by surface forms. A CX:AES (Agent-Executable Specification) Codex has three constitutionally distinct layers: CX-S — domain physics: what must hold in every valid instance (invariants, inadmissible regions) CX-C — configuration: what was chosen from the possibility space and why (selections, rationale, blast radius) CX-I — realization: how to construct or instantiate the system given CX-S constraints and CX-C decisions

metadata.sourceExcerpt: Intent: Ensure every analytical output explicitly states what it does not determine, preventing downstream use that exceeds the output's evidential scope. Grounding: CG-03 (Non-Guarantee Clause) — every framework construct explicitly bounds what it does NOT guarantee. P-1 is CG-03 applied operationally to practitioner outputs. Structure: 1. Produce the analytical output (gate receipt, crystallization, assessment, etc.) 2. Before considering the output complete, ask: "What does this output NOT determine?" 3. State the non-guarantee explicitly as a named field or section of the output record: - What question does this output leave open? - What downstream conclusions would it be incorrect to draw? - What measurement or confirmation does not exist yet? 4. The non-guarantee statement is part of the output, not an optional addition. Applied in: Every component in every phase. Explicitly required in: C-01 (does not determine admissibility or inertia), C-04 (does not determine what path forward is correct), C-06 (no measurement protocol; domain-relative), C-08 (property vocabulary is configuration, not guarantee of meaning), C-11 (basin membership ≠ correctness), C-12 (qualitative only), C-20 (SGC is a theoretical limit), C-21 (approximate detection only), C-22 (PROVISIONAL), C-23 (compatibility ≠ equivalence; PROVISIONAL). Anti-patterns: *Silent non-guarantee:* producing an output without stating what it does not determine. A receipt without a non-guarantee section implies completeness it does not have. *Non-guarantee as disclaimer:* appending "this is not legal advice" style language without specifying what the particular output does not determine. The non-guarantee must be specific to the output, not generic. *Non-guarantee that undermines the output:* stating "this output determines nothing" or "all conclusions are uncertain" violates the spirit of CG-03 — the goal is honest scoping, not epistemic collapse. State precisely what IS determined and what IS NOT. ---

metadata.sourceExcerpt: *Source: OSP Inertia — Symmetric Transition Law. Derived from R23, empirically confirmed.* Statement: The cost to create a semantic bridge between two artifacts equals the cost to dissolve it. Adding one shared entry costs one unit; removing it costs one unit. Semantic bridge formation and dissolution are symmetric under the unit cost metric. Enforcement implication: There is no ratchet effect in semantic distance. Every bridge built can be dissolved at equal cost. Inertia assessments (C-06) must therefore look at network embeddedness, not just the cost of the last operation. Violation detection: Under SP-06 (atomicity), both creation and dissolution costs are exactly one unit by definition. SP-08 violations are structural defects in the cost accounting model, not observable in normal operation. Relationship to governance layer: Grounds O-16 (Semantic Binding Quality) — SBQ cannot be inferred from creation cost, since dissolution costs the same. SBQ is a structural property (does this binding carry load?), not a cost property. Also grounds O-27 (Parasitic Binding) — parasitic bindings are not distinguishable from load-bearing bindings by creation cost; only structural load distinguishes them. ---

RPZ2.intension: The cost to create a semantic bridge between two artifacts equals the cost to dissolve it. Adding one shared entry costs one unit; removing it costs one unit. Semantic bridge formation and dissolution are symmetric under the unit cost metric.

metadata.sourceExcerpt: What it does (PROVISIONAL): Examines a system's crystallization receipt chain for boundary-theater patterns (O-56) — admission receipts whose corresponding gate-predicate evaluation receipts are absent or synthetic. Detection requires meta-receipt audit (per OQ-11): for each admission event, verify a corresponding gate- evaluation receipt with non-trivial predicate evaluation content. Inputs: System receipt chain + crystallization boundary declarations + gate predicate specifications Outputs: Theater detection report — confirmed theater / no theater / undetectable (gate-evaluation receipts not produced) + affected boundary set Invariants enforced: - CG-04 (Admissibility Precedes Effect, including v1.8 crystallization- receipt sub-clause): boundary theater violates CG-04 substantively while satisfying it formally - CG-08 (Governed Evidence Source Preference): detection requires reading from the receipt chain (gate-evaluation evidence), not from in-memory or runtime state Status: PROVISIONAL — pending O-56 promotion and OQ-11 (meta- receipt of gate evaluation) resolution. Constructs invoked: O-56 (Boundary as Theater, PROVISIONAL), O-04 (Admissibility Gate), O-32 (Receipt Stratification) ---

metadata.sourceExcerpt: Observation: O-56 (Boundary as Theater, PROVISIONAL in v1.8) names the failure mode in which crystallization rituals are performed without genuine gate-predicate evaluation. Receipts exist; the gate did not actually evaluate. Detection requires meta-receipt: a receipt of the gate's evaluation, not merely a receipt of the admission outcome. The frontier: What is the structural specification of a meta- receipt? Candidates: A receipt recording the gate's predicate evaluation steps (predicate-level audit trail) A receipt recording the gate's input artifact hash and the gate's output verdict, without the intermediate evaluation steps A receipt recording structural evidence that the gate executed non-trivially (e.g., that the predicate evaluation was bound to a specific authority, that the predicate was non-vacuous) The candidates differ in what they detect: predicate-level audit trails detect manipulation of evaluation logic; input-output receipts detect tampering with the verdict; non-triviality evidence detects predicates that always return ALLOW. What a meta-receipt specification would need to specify: The minimum evidence required to distinguish genuine evaluation from theater The substrate cost of meta-receipt production (production overhead; storage cost; chain-bloat implications) The compatibility with existing CG-04 (Admissibility Precedes Effect) enforcement — is meta-receipt a new layer atop admissibility, or embedded in it? The interaction with C-33 (Boundary Theater Detection, PROVISIONAL) — what evidence does C-33 read? Status: OPEN. Promoted to OQ-11 from B.1-OQ-14 candidate slate. Affects: O-56 (Boundary as Theater) promotion to ADMISSIBLE contingent on this resolution; C-33 methodology specification. ---

metadata.sourceExcerpt: Definition: The set difference *R(I) \\ C(S)*: the realization paths an invariant requires but the specification does not constrain. The region in which plausible-but-wrong implementations (O-40) can survive specification scrutiny while violating intent. A specification with zero saturation gap is fully saturated for its invariant; a specification with non-zero gap admits realizations that satisfy the specification's plain reading while violating its intent. The saturation gap may be either a defect gap (an unintended realization region the specification fails to constrain) or a tolerable ambiguity (O-43, a deliberately preserved region of agent discretion). The two are governance-relevant distinct: defect gaps require closure; tolerable ambiguity must be explicitly declared. Domain: Specification / Realization Depends on: O-37 (Realization Surface), O-38 (Constraint Surface) Primary source: Admissibility_Engineering.md (forthcoming) Razor classification: Expansion. Toll: (a) insufficiency — existing ARC had no language for the realization-versus-constraint surface gap; (b) new degree of freedom — saturation as a measurable property enabling ideal-saturation as a design target; (c) rollback criterion — if no working system demonstrates that closing the gap improves convergence (O-44), demote to Exploration. Invariant relationships: Grounds the discipline of admissibility engineering (Pattern P-5) Subject of CG-07 (Convergence-As-Measurement): convergence rates decline as saturation gaps widen; closing gaps raises convergence Non-guarantee: The saturation gap is not in general computable from the specification alone; it must be characterized empirically by observing realizations that survive specification while violating intent. Closure requires relocating constraints from instruction-layer to artifact-layer (catalog of techniques, Pattern P-5). Contrast: Saturation gap ≠ specification incompleteness. Incompleteness names the absence of specification on some matter; saturation gap names the shortfall of constraint surface relative to the realization surface of declared invariants. metadata.sourceExcerpt: Definition: A failure mode in which generated code is structurally valid, type- correct, syntactically well-formed, and superficially aligned with the specification, yet behaves divergently from specification intent. The dominant failure mode of agentic coding above the complexity threshold (O-41). Distinguished from hallucination (which produces non-existent references and typically fails at compile time) and syntax error (which fails parsing). Plausible-but-wrong realizations are valid syntactically, valid type-wise, and surface-plausible behaviorally; they survive unit testing because unit tests verify only the realizations the test author thought to enumerate. Domain: Failure Modes / Realization Depends on: O-09 (CBI), O-39 (Saturation Gap) Primary source: Admissibility_Engineering.md (forthcoming) Status: ADMISSIBLE (promoted v1.9; AE primary source + structural distinction from O-18 + working-deployment empirical anchor jointly sufficient per v1.9 candidate slate review) Razor classification: Expansion (named failure class). Cross-paper signals: Indirect support from O-18 (Corruption as Illegitimate Continuation) — both are continuation failures; one in the semantic layer (O-18), one in the realization layer (this construct). The structural distinction from O-18 (under-saturation vs authority laundering) is operationally load-bearing: Corruption requires governance repair; PBW requires specification saturation. v1.9 promotion record: Promoted from PROVISIONAL to ADMISSIBLE under v1.9 candidate slate disposition. C-30 (Plausible-But-Wrong Detection) component status follows. ---

metadata.sourceExcerpt: *Source: OSP Force — Divergence Gradient. Derived from R24, empirically confirmed.* Statement: The natural direction of semantic motion under independent growth is away from other artifacts, not toward them. For any two artifacts developing independently, each new vocabulary addition increases their exclusive-entry count. The gradient points outward: toward greater separation, not toward overlap. Enforcement implication: Any analysis expecting convergence without detecting a coordination mechanism is analytically incomplete. If two independent agents are expected to maintain semantic alignment, that alignment requires a governance mechanism — it will not maintain itself. Violation detection: If independent artifact development produces decreasing exclusive-entry counts without intersection- targeted additions, SP-13 is violated at the observation level. This indicates either the artifacts are not actually independent or the diff analysis has an error. Relationship to governance layer: Grounds CG-05 (Authority Must Be Declared) — authority declarations are the governance response to SP-13; without declared authority, independent agents diverge by default and the divergence is invisible. Also grounds CG-02 (Cannot Proceed Silently) — ungoverned divergence under SP-13 is the physics that makes silent continuation harmful. ---

metadata.sourceExcerpt: *Reclassified from INV-02. Constitutional governance invariant.* Statement: Any governance-relevant transition of a semantic artifact must be receipted. A system in the Ableman framework cannot make admissibility decisions, authority bindings, or semantic transitions without producing a receipt that records what was decided, under what authority, and with what result. Receipts are the proof; execution without receipts is ungoverned motion. Enforcement implication: Every pipeline stage, gate evaluation, authority binding, and corpus integration must produce a receipt. An analysis that produces outputs without receipted decisions has ungoverned motion. This applies equally to stopping conditions: a REFUSE without a receipt is an ungoverned refusal. Violation detection: Violated when any governance-relevant decision is made without a corresponding receipt. Detection: receipt chain gaps, downstream components consuming outputs from unreceipted decisions, conformance snapshots citing analytical conclusions without tracing them to receipted gate evaluations. Physics grounding: SP-09 (Shared Core Persistence) — receipts are durable in the same way shared semantic structure is durable; once created, they persist under additive development. SP-03 (Containment Under Refinement) — the receipt chain is an additive record; silent continuation breaks the containment property of the lineage. SP-04 (Divergence Under Parallel Expansion) — without receipts, parallel development diverges without trace; receipts make the divergence gradient visible and governable. Enforcement mechanism: LineageChain in OSP core/lineage.py. Receipt chain verification in validation/chain.py. C-02 receipt requirement in Phase B. DI-G2 across all OSP phases (receipts non-optional). ---

metadata.sourceExcerpt: Primitive statement: Every governance-relevant act is performed under explicitly declared authority. Authority cannot be ambient, inherited, or assumed from context — it must be named, bounded, and recorded in the receipt. ARC anchors: CG-05 (Authority Must Be Declared): the invariant. Profile implication: ACI-06 prevents authority laundering through ambient or assumed authority. A deployment satisfying P1 has explicit authority declarations on every governance event; missing declarations mean the deployment has implicit authority somewhere, which is structurally inadmissible. Cryptographic realization across the framework (added v1.9.5): ACI-06 names the discipline (authority must be declared); the framework consistently selects *public-key-derived identity* as the cryptographic realization of authority across substrates that admit cryptographic construction. Observable instances: MIP §3.1 (Mosaic ID): network-endpoint identity = hash(authority pubkey) DKN dimension construction (D-1): dimension_id = blake3(phase_code || authority_pubkey); namespace identity bound to authority's private key Cryptographic Phase epoch keys: epoch authorization via authority signature; regime-level identity DKN sealable dimensions (D-7): finalization through provable key burning; authority commitment via cryptographic destruction These are not coincidentally similar implementations. They are the same primitive — public-key-derived identity — applied at different layers (network endpoints, namespaces, regimes, finalizations). Distinction: ACI-06 names the *governance discipline* (authority must be declared, not ambient or inherited). The cryptographic realization is the *structural pattern* the framework consistently selects when constructing this discipline cryptographically. Non-cryptographic substrates (e.g., conventional document codices) realize ACI-06 through declaration in the artifact text rather than through cryptographic key binding. The realization varies; the discipline is invariant. metadata.sourceExcerpt: Observation: Admissibility Engineering (per AE) names ambiguity engineering as the natural complement: the discipline of declaring tolerable ambiguity (O-43) explicitly and bounding it. AE §8 frames this as the natural next research direction. Whether ambiguity engineering warrants admission as a distinct discipline (with its own constructs, invariants, methods) is held open. The frontier: Admissibility engineering closes saturation gaps through artifact-layer constraints. Ambiguity engineering would *declare* tolerable ambiguity regions structurally, distinguishing them from defect gaps. The two disciplines compose: a saturation gap is either closed (admissibility engineering) or declared (ambiguity engineering). What admission would require: A primary-source paper for ambiguity engineering as a named discipline (currently AE §2.5 and §8 mention it; no dedicated paper exists) Construct definitions for ambiguity-engineering-specific structures (analogous to O-37, O-38, O-39 for admissibility engineering) Failure modes (analogous to O-40 Plausible-But-Wrong) for over- ambiguity: tolerable-ambiguity declarations that mask actual defect gaps Methods for distinguishing the two disciplines in practice — when to close versus when to declare Status: OPEN. Promoted to OQ-12 from B.1-OQ-15 candidate slate. Defer until first primary-source paper exists. Affects: Future ARC versions; O-43 (Tolerable Ambiguity) promotion contingent on the discipline maturing. ---

metadata.sourceExcerpt: Statement: Performing the rituals of crystallization (creating receipts, naming authorities, declaring scopes) without enforcing the underlying admissibility evaluation is inadmissible. Receipts produced without genuine gate-predicate evaluation are forged; they pollute the receipt chain with audit-meaningless content while preserving the appearance of governance. Source: Constitutional_Semantic_Crystallization (consolidated, forthcoming) §7.5; ARC entry O-56 (Boundary as Theater, PROVISIONAL). Structural reason: Boundary theater satisfies CG-02 (Cannot Proceed Silently — receipts exist) and superficially satisfies CG-04 (Admissibility Precedes Effect — admission events are recorded), but violates the spirit of both because the gate predicates were not actually evaluated. The receipts are formally correct and substantively meaningless. Auditing the chain reveals admission events; auditing the *gate* would reveal that no evaluation occurred. Detection requires meta-receipts of gate evaluation (see OQ-11). Detection: A system in this region produces admission receipts whose corresponding gate-predicate evaluation receipts are absent or synthetic. Audit: for each admission event, verify a corresponding gate-evaluation receipt exists with non-trivial predicate evaluation content. Adjacency: Genuine crystallization (O-55, O-04, CG-04) is the adjacent admissible region. The distinguishing factor is whether the gate predicate was actually evaluated against the proposed artifact; the same receipt structure can record either evaluation or theater, depending on whether the substrate produced it through genuine evaluation. ---

metadata.sourceExcerpt: Intent: Prevent the conflation of observational evidence (signal — what was observed) with structural interpretation (structure — what the observation means in the framework). The two require different analytical handling and produce different kinds of receipts. Grounding: CG-06 (Governance Operates on Structure, Not Narrative) — structural criteria govern admissibility decisions; narrative signal does not. P-2 is CG-06 operationalized as an input-handling discipline. Structure: 1. When assembling inputs for any component, classify each input as: - Signal: raw observation, behavioral evidence, empirical record — something observed about the domain. Signal does not carry authority; it requires structural interpretation before it can influence analytical conclusions. - Structure: a declared constraint, a crystallized MCIR artifact, a gate receipt, a typed artifact record — something already governed by the framework. Structure carries authority from its production receipt. 2. Apply different handling to each class: - Signal inputs are evaluated against declared constraints before they can ground conclusions (they must pass C-02 admissibility evaluation). - Structure inputs are used directly as analytical inputs (they carry their own provenance and receipts). 3. Never treat signal as structure — observational evidence does not automatically become a framework fact. It must be crystallized (C-08) before it has structural status. 4. Never treat structure as mere signal — a crystallized MCIR artifact is not "just evidence" to be weighed; it is a governed fact with receipted provenance. Applied in: C-02 (evaluating artifact against constraint — the artifact is signal until admitted), C-07 (proposed inference chain is signal; F_C is structure), C-08 (PCM is signal candidate; MCIR is structure output), C-15 (observations are signal; corruption pattern taxonomy is structure), C-17 (behavior record is signal; ESA capacities are structural criteria). A Governance Coverage Gap exists when: (1) A governance model declares N independent specification layers as applicable to operations of type T (N ≥ 2); (2) In a specific execution of an operation of type T, only k < N layers participate in evaluation (k ≥ 0); (3) The execution record does not explicitly state that N−k layers were declared applicable but did not participate. The result: the artifact record presents k-layer governance as if it were complete governance. A reader cannot distinguish "all N applicable layers evaluated and allowed" from "k of N applicable layers evaluated and allowed; N−k layers were not consulted." Admissibility constraint: Governance Coverage Gap assertions are only admissible when the declared applicable specification set N can be stated or approximated. Where N cannot be determined, only Coverage Gap suspicion may be recorded, not a formal O-35 assertion. An analyst who cannot state N cannot produce an admissible O-35 claim — they can note that multi-layer governance was possible but cannot assert which layers were absent. Three named forms of the gap: 1. Layer Non-Activation — a specification layer applicable to the operation family is not enforced in this execution context (the layer exists in the governance model; it was not active in this context). 2. Layer Absence — a specification layer applicable to the operation family is not present in this execution context (the layer is declared as part of the governance model; it was not instantiated here). 3. Layer Bypass — a specification layer applicable to the operation family was present and active but the execution path did not pass through it (the layer is present; the specific execution routed around it without record of the routing).
