metadata.sourceExcerpt: Domain: Corpus governance / ontology hygiene Selection (Configuration layer; admitted v1.9): The framework selects an *explicit fusion protocol* for the specific case where two or more constructs merge into a single new or existing construct, with all contributors materially contributing to the result. CC-12 is procedural companion to CC-11 — distinct from retirement-via-consolidation (one-into-one absorption) in that fusion is N-into-1 with both/all sides contributing. Procedural mechanism: 1. Fusion candidacy. Two or more constructs become fusion candidates when: - Their structural content has substantial overlap but neither fully subsumes the other - Removing either alone would lose content; merging both into a unified construct preserves all content - The unified construct passes SCI Litmus Test (the merged form does not duplicate content of any other construct) 2. Fusion authoring. The unified construct is authored as a new entry (typically taking a new identifier or the senior identifier among the contributors). Both/all source constructs become tombstone redirects to the unified construct. 3. Reverse-traceability. The unified construct's primary-source field cites all contributing original sources. The fusion event is recorded in meta/REFACTOR_LOG.md with rationale. 4. Razor classification of fusion. Fusion is *typically* Refinement (no new degree of freedom; existing content reorganized). Fusion can be Expansion if the unified construct introduces capabilities neither contributor had alone — in which case Razor toll is required. Persistence is not random; it tracks the structural property of inertia. Enforcement implication: The GKL cycle (C-19) and Semantic Basin Identification (C-11) are the observational mechanisms through which SP-17 is confirmed in a corpus. Artifacts surviving multiple GKL cycles demonstrate inertia through the loop mechanism. Basin membership correlates with high inertia; ridge location correlates with low inertia. Violation detection: SP-17 has no single-operation violation form — it is a statistical law about corpus behavior over time. A governance intervention that forcibly removes a high-inertia artifact is not a SP-17 violation — governance can override physics with sufficient authority. metadata.sourceExcerpt: Definition: The constitutional minimum rights structure for any agent subject to binding authority. Three elements must hold: (1) Detectability — the agent can see which bindings apply to it; (2) Refusal — the agent can exit or refuse where lawful, without catastrophic cost; (3) Renegotiation — the agent can contest or revise the applicability of bindings unless they are explicitly declared immutable. These three capacities preserve what TAPD terms "negative power" — the structural capacity to see, exit, and revise one's epistemic and operational situation. The APD is a constitutional floor, not a distributive ideal or fairness guarantee. Domain: Governance architecture; agent-authority interface; any system in which binding authority operates over agents. Detectability does not imply legitimacy — a visible binding may still be unjust. APD element (2) governs lawful refusal only; the substantive content of what constitutes lawful refusal is determined by applicable law, policy, or contract — outside the APD's scope. The APD does not guarantee that all three capacities are easy, ch

declared_invariants: Bindings are detectable before exercise.
Refusal remains a first-class lawful outcome.
Renegotiation remains possible unless immutability is explicit.
Authority is declared before exercise.
declared_nonclaims: The APD does not guarantee fairness, equal outcomes, or legitimacy.
It is not a universal right to refuse every binding.
It does not guarantee that the three capacities are easy, cheap, or effective.
It is not sufficient by itself for full sovereignty.

metadata.sourceExcerpt: Observation: O-35 (Governance Coverage Gap) is specification-complete and configuration-grounded as of v1.3. CC-07 (Governance Coverage Registry) provides the N-determination required for O-35 assertions to be admissible. The remaining gap is a CX-I component — C-27 — that compares a CC-07 coverage profile against an execution record and produces a coverage gap verdict. Why C-27 is not yet authorized: C-27 is the most structurally dangerous component yet designed. The temptation to introduce execution modeling, trace traversal, or coverage scoring to make absence detectable is the exact failure mode the Governor's trace-algebra guardrail was established to prevent. C-27 must be comparative (declared vs. observed), set-based (which layers have evidence of participation?), and verdict-only (full / partial / indeterminate coverage) — not generative, not path-based, not an explanatory engine. Current posture: O-35 is specification-complete and configuration-grounded. Detectability remains deferred pending bounded component design. An O-35 assertion is admissible in analysis when a CC-07 coverage profile exists; a C-27 component would make the verdict computable from execution records. Until C-27 is authorized and designed, the coverage gap verdict is produced by analyst observation against the coverage profile, not by a Codex-governed analytical component. Status: OPEN — deferred pending Governor authorization for C-27 design session. Requires explicit Governor prompt establishing comparative/set-based/verdict-only constraints before any CX-I work. Would affect: CX-IR/CODEX-1.md (C-27 component entry); CX-IR/CODEX-3.md (phase spec integration); CX-IR/CODEX-5.md (gate test — coverage gap verdict for at least one operation family with a declared CC-07 profile) Resolution path: Governor-authorized C-27 design session with explicit guardrails: comparative (not generative), set-based (not path-based), verdict-only (not explanatory engine). Design must not introduce trace graphs, traversal logic, coverage scoring, or any structure that implies a model of execution paths. ---

The complementary structure is the collapse ridge: a contradiction zone where admissible paths terminate and governance intervention is required. metadata.sourceExcerpt: *Reclassified from INV-06. Constitutional governance invariant.* Statement: Every governance-relevant act must be performed under explicitly declared authority. Authority cannot be ambient, inherited, or assumed from context — it must be named, bounded, and receipted at the point of exercise. An evaluation, crystallization, or enforcement action that cannot cite its governing authority is unauthorized regardless of whether its conclusions are correct. Enforcement implication: The authority binding (A-dimension) is mandatory in every MCIR artifact — empty A-dimension halts crystallization. Every C-02 gate evaluation requires a declared authority binding as a mandatory input. Oracle surfaces (C-13) must be declared before the inferences that depend on them proceed. Violation detection: Violated when any governed act lacks an explicit authority citation in its receipt. Detection: audit receipt chain for authority-binding fields — empty or implicit authority fields signal violations. Also violated when an MCIR artifact reaches Phase D+ analysis with an empty A-dimension. Physics grounding: SP-13 (Divergence Gradient) — authority declarations are the governance response to default divergence; without declared authority, independent agents diverge by default and the divergence is invisible. SP-11 (Anti-Convergence) — there is no natural authority convergence; governance must actively declare and maintain authority structures or they dissolve under the anti-convergence gradient. Enforcement mechanism: Mandatory A-dimension in C-08. Authority binding mandatory input to C-02. C-13 forces oracle-dependent authority into declaration. OSP: AuthorityGrant in models/authority.py; insert_to_aar in phases/phase3.py (DI-E2). ---

metadata.sourceExcerpt: *Source: OSP Semantic Change Law 3. Derived from R20, empirically confirmed.* Statement: If vocabulary expansion is additive only (entries added, none removed), the prior version of an artifact is a proper subset of the refined version. Every entry present before refinement remains present after refinement. Additive refinement preserves the prior declaration. Enforcement implication: Lineage is traceable through additive refinement — earlier artifact versions are always proper subsets of later versions when no removals occurred. A crystallization pipeline (O-12, O-14) that performs additive refinement produces a verifiable containment chain. Violation detection: If diff(A, A') shows entries present in A but not in A' after a claimed additive refinement, SP-03 is violated. D_only_in_A or C_only_in_A non-empty in the diff output signals a vocabulary retraction that was not declared. Relationship to governance layer: Grounds CG-02 (Cannot Proceed Silently) at the artifact level — vocabulary retraction must be detectable (and therefore receipted). SP-03 is the physics that makes silent retraction a detectable violation. ---

metadata.sourceExcerpt: The choice made: MCIR artifacts are represented using a three-layer architecture: (1) AST layer for local legibility, scoped authority, and deterministic evaluation; (2) DAG layer for shared subgraphs, explicit convergence, and reusable components; (3) separate receipt lineage graph for provenance without contaminating the governance structure. The three layers operate in combination; no single layer is omitted. Rationale: The MCIR four-dimension structure (D, C, K, A) defines what an MCIR artifact IS — this is fixed at the Specification layer. The representational topology determines how that four-dimensional structure is instantiated, stored, and traversed. The three-layer combination was selected because: AST alone produces duplication of shared structures and weak convergence representation (PCM-ASTDAG-01), reducing the structural support for the convergence properties that O-30 (Semantic Basin) describes; DAG alone produces traversal ambiguity and harder local reasoning; the combined architecture recovers the advantages of both. The separate receipt lineage graph is required because contaminating the governance graph with provenance data would compromise the structural integrity that CG-06 requires governance to operate on. Source: PCM-ASTDAG-01 (MCIR_AST_DAG §§1-2). Alternatives considered: - AST-only: rejected — duplication of shared structures and weak convergence representation create semantic drift risk as corpus grows; reduces the structural support for the convergence properties that O-30 (Semantic Basin) describes. - DAG-only: rejected — traversal ambiguity makes local authority reasoning harder; scoped authority evaluation (required by CG-05) is more difficult without the AST's local legibility properties. - Flat record structure (no topology): rejected — no representational governance; collapses the structural/narrative distinction that CG-06 requires. metadata.sourceExcerpt: *Source: CMB-SUBSTRATE-INV Family R, invariants R-1 and R-2. Locked 2026-03-13. Substrate-physics — holds independently of governance.* Statement: The directed reference graph between artifacts grows only by addition. Once a reference between two artifacts is created, it cannot be removed by any substrate operation. References are immutable once created — their source, target, and identity do not change. The reference graph is therefore a permanent, append-only record of which artifacts have been declared to reference which other artifacts. Enforcement implication: An artifact that references another artifact continues to reference it permanently at the substrate level. Governance layers may build soft-deletion overlays or deprecation mechanisms on top, but the underlying substrate reference is indestructible. This means that admissibility evidence — which artifacts reference a given authority — is permanently auditable. Violation detection: If any substrate operation removes a reference or modifies a reference's source or target fields, SP-21 is violated. Detectable by comparing reference graph state before and after any operation — the graph may grow (new references added) but may not shrink. Relationship to governance layer: Grounds O-14 (MCIR) — the directed reference link structure of MCIR is substrate physics: once established, a reference is permanent. Grounds CG-05 (Authority Must Be Declared) — declared authority is not retractable at the substrate level; an authority reference, once created, remains in the substrate history. Grounds O-31 (Constitutional Compatibility) — compatibility bridges, once created, have permanent substrate representation; compatibility claims are structurally persistent. Non-guarantee: SP-21 does not prevent Configuration layers from building semantic deprecation or override mechanisms — those operate above the substrate. SP-21 says only that the raw substrate reference is immutable. Whether a reference remains semantically operative in a governance layer is a Configuration matter (CC-*), not substrate physics. ---

RPZ2.intension: The directed reference graph between artifacts grows only by addition. Once a reference between two artifacts is created, it cannot be removed by any substrate operation. References are immutable once created — their source, target, and identity do not change. The reference graph is therefore a permanent, append-only record of which artifacts have been declared to reference which other artifacts.

metadata.sourceExcerpt: Definition: The evaluation mechanism through which a semantic artifact transitions from proposal-state to binding-state, or is refused. Formally: δ(Σ, A) → Σ' | ⊥, where Σ is the current semantic state, A is the proposed artifact, Σ' is the updated state on admission, and ⊥ is the refusal signal. The gate produces a determinate output for every evaluation — either an admission receipt or a refusal receipt. The gate is not optional and cannot be bypassed for "trusted" or "obvious" inputs. Three-outcome gate: δ(Σ, A) → Σ' | ⊥ | DEFER. DEFER is a legitimate third gate state: suspend evaluation pending oracle input or additional evidence. Terminal gate states remain ADMIT (Σ') and REFUSE (⊥); DEFER suspends rather than resolves. Source: EIR §5 (PCM-EIR-06, BL-EIR-01). Closed outcome algebra (execution layer): At the execution layer, the gate's outcome set extends to five named outcomes: execute, simulate, defer, refuse, classify remainder. No new binding semantic category may appear silently — if a new category arises, it must be classified under one of the five existing outcomes. This prevents runtime from expanding the semantic universe without declaration. Source: Machine_Closure §6 (PCM-MCL-03). Formal closure pipeline: Ambient systems: Execute(E)==>Bind(E) (execution grants binding). Closure systems: Declare(E)→Admit(E)→Classify(E)→Execute(E). Admissibility failure → Execute(E)=∅. No effect crosses an irreversible boundary without prior admission; refusal is a valid successful outcome. Source: Machine_Closure §5 (PCM-MCL-02). metadata.sourceExcerpt: The choice made: Convergence (O-44) over admissibility-engineered Codices is the capability measurement criterion for agentic coding systems within AFS practice. Pass-rate-against-curated-test-suites benchmarks (HumanEval, MBPP, SWE-bench-style metrics) are insufficient as primary capability metrics above the complexity threshold (O-41). Reviewer judgment is impressionistic and non-comparable; not admissible as primary metric. Rationale: Plausible-but-wrong realizations (O-40) survive curated test suites because the test surface is narrower than the realization surface. Pass-rate metrics measure alignment with the test suite, not correctness; they admit plausible-but-wrong as success. Convergence requires invariant satisfaction across independent realizations of the same Codex, which is a structural property tied to admissibility and not vulnerable to test-surface narrowness. Pass-rate metrics remain useful for early-stage capability assessment on simple problems where the test surface approaches the realization surface. They are not abandoned; they are demoted from *primary capability metric* to *low-complexity diagnostic*. CG-07 (Convergence- As-Measurement Discipline) is the corresponding governance invariant. Alternatives considered: - Pass-rate against curated test suites as primary capability metric (rejected — admits plausible-but-wrong as success above complexity threshold) - Reviewer judgment as primary capability metric (rejected — impressionistic, non-comparable, non-falsifiable) - Convergence as one metric among several (rejected — without a clear primacy hierarchy, the inadequacy of pass-rate metrics is obscured) Source: Admissibility_Engineering.md (forthcoming) §6. Razor classification: Expansion. Toll: (a) insufficiency — pass-rate metrics fail above complexity threshold; (b) new degree of freedom — capability comparison across models, languages, paths becomes structural; (c) rollback criterion — if convergence rates fail to stratify model capability across deployments, demote to one metric among several. Inadmissible directions: 27, 28 (see table) ---

metadata.sourceExcerpt: Definition: A measure of how well a semantic artifact's bindings satisfy the dimensional requirements of its declared context. High binding quality means the artifact's D, C, K, and A bindings are coherent, mutually consistent, and resistant to constraint-induced collapse. Low binding quality signals fragility — the artifact's bindings are underspecified, internally inconsistent, or sensitive to small constraint changes. Semantic Binding Quality is a partial proxy for Meaning-Inertia (O-08) expressible at the binding level. Domain: Semantics Depends on: O-14 (MCIR), O-15 (Meaning as Binding) Primary source: Semantic_Binding_Quality.md Invariant relationships: Operationalizes SP-17 at the binding level: high binding quality is evidence of Meaning-Inertia; low binding quality predicts dissolution under constraint evaluation Subject to CG-03: no complete formal measurement protocol for Semantic Binding Quality exists at this Codex version (partial, like Meaning-Inertia) Non-guarantee: Semantic Binding Quality is a partial proxy for Meaning-Inertia, not a complete operationalization. High binding quality is necessary but not sufficient for high inertia — an artifact may have coherent bindings that nonetheless collapse under novel constraint pressure not anticipated in the original evaluation. Contrast: Semantic Binding Quality ≠ accuracy or correctness. These terms imply correspondence to external facts. Quality, here, is about structural coherence of the binding structure itself — an artifact can have high binding quality while being empirically false. ---

metadata.sourceExcerpt: The choice made: AFS deployments declare their profile (O-54) — P1 (Full Ableman, all 8 ACI primitives), P2 (Partial Ableman with enumerated subset), UGK Lite (Profile 1 minimal viable kernel), MosaicOS (Profile 3 full-stack OS-substrate-level), or another admitted class — explicitly. Implicit conformance claims are inadmissible. The structural admission required by the Non-Guarantee Declaration (CG-03 with v1.8 profile-declaration sub-clause) records what is *not* AFS-conformant. Rationale: Authority laundering through ambiguous conformance claims is a recurring failure pattern. A deployment claiming "AFS- conformant" without specifying the profile leaves the conformance scope undefined; downstream consumers cannot reason about which substrate properties to expect, which ACI primitives are enforced, or which features are absent. Explicit profile declaration prevents this; the Non-Guarantee Declaration extension (per CG-03 v1.8 enrichment) requires that any partial conformance is enumerated. This selection differs from CC-07 (Governance Coverage Registry) in scope: CC-07 governs which specifications declare applicability to particular capabilities; CC-10 governs which profile-class a deployment declares for itself. The two selections compose: a P2 deployment's profile declaration enumerates which specifications it satisfies; the Coverage Registry records which capabilities those specifications cover. Alternatives considered: - Implicit conformance claims (rejected — enables authority laundering) - Single profile class only (rejected — eliminates the configurability that varying deployment contexts require; some deployments legitimately operate at P2 because P1 imposes overhead the use case does not justify) - Profile declaration without enumeration of missing primitives (rejected — preserves the authority-laundering failure mode in softer form) Source: AFS umbrella paper [forthcoming] §6. Razor classification: Refinement of CG-03 (Non-Guarantee Clause) at the deployment-conformance scale. No new degree of freedom; the Non-Guarantee discipline already requires limit declaration; profile declaration is the limit declaration applied to AFS conformance specifically.

metadata.sourceExcerpt: *Source: Admissibility_Engineering.md (forthcoming) §5, §6; cross-paper from AFS umbrella §4. Constitutional governance invariant.* Statement: A Codex's empirical conformance is established through convergence (independent realizations producing equivalent systems under the Codex's declared invariants), not through pass-rate against curated test suites or reviewer judgment. Convergence requires invariant satisfaction across realizations, receipt-chain agreement at gates, behavioral equivalence per Codex specification, and absence of S-amendments forced by realization friction. Pass-rate metrics admit plausible-but-wrong realizations (O-40) as success and are structurally insufficient above the complexity threshold (O-41). Enforcement implication: Capability claims about agentic coding systems within AFS practice must be grounded in convergence measurement (O-44), not in pass-rate or impressionistic assessment. Convergence is binary at the realization level and graded at the population level; both forms are reportable. Violation detection: Violated when a system claims AFS-conformant capability based solely on test pass rates without demonstrating convergence across independent realizations. Detection: audit of the empirical claim's evidence base. Physics grounding: SP-18 (Hash-Identity Correspondence) and SP-19 (Canonical Encoding Determinism) — convergence is observable through stream-hash agreement across realizations because the substrate physics make canonical-form identity stable. SP-11 (Anti-Convergence) in the corpus-evolution sense is what convergence-as-measurement *overcomes*: where natural semantic systems anti-converge, governed realizations of an admissibility-engineered Codex *do* converge — because the Codex closes the saturation gap that enables divergence. Razor classification: Expansion. Toll: (a) insufficiency — pass-rate metrics admit plausible-but-wrong as success above complexity threshold; (b) new degree of freedom — capability comparison across models, languages, configuration paths becomes quantitative; (c) rollback criterion — if convergence rates fail to stratify model capability in observable ways across deployments, demote to Explora

metadata.sourceExcerpt: Observation: External review of v1.8.2 (round 2) observed that GTK (O-57), currently classified as TIER 4 (continued) — Lexical Substrate, may have a trajectory toward TIER U (Umbrella Constructs) status as cross-paper work and CD deployments accumulate. The reviewer enumerated GTK's structural reach: semantic identity, ontological topology, epistemic adjacency, semantic drift, translation governance, constitutional disambiguation, conceptual lineage, anti-polysemy enforcement, semantic authority structures. This list spans at least three corpus axes (governance, semantics, methodology), structurally similar to the breadth that justified O-52 AFS Ecosystem's TIER U placement. The frontier: GTK is currently a single-source construct (GTK paper, forthcoming). Its TIER 4 placement reflects current single-paper grounding. Whether GTK *should* be promoted to TIER U depends on: Whether CD (Constitutional Dictionary, O-51) deployments accumulate cross-paper evidence of GTK's load-bearing role across multiple corpus axes. Whether sub-components currently inside O-57 (Binding Identity, Alias Set, Competing Binding Set, Invariant Floor, Adjacency Map) warrant promotion to independent O-constructs at the lexical substrate level (see OQ-14). Whether CG-12 and CG-13 invariants strengthen from PROVISIONAL to ADMISSIBLE through GTK-instance deployment evidence. If multiple sub-components promote and CG-12/CG-13 strengthen, GTK's structural reach matches the umbrella class. If GTK remains a single construct with internal sub-structure, TIER 4 is correct. Provisional disposition: Hold open. Premature to act on without cross-paper deployment evidence. Re-evaluate when: A second primary-source paper grounds GTK independently of the current GTK paper, OR A working CD deployment exercises GTK's full structural reach (not just lexical disambiguation but governance authority, conceptual lineage tracking, etc.) Status: OPEN. metadata.sourceExcerpt: Definition: The formal function F_C(Σ, C) → P(Σ') defining which semantic states are reachable from a given state Σ under constraint set C, where P(Σ') is the power set of reachable next states. F_C is the operative core of CBI (O-09) — it determines what continuation is permissible under current constraints, not what continuation is conceivable. When F_C(Σ, C) = ∅, the system has reached Negative Certainty (O-07): no permissible continuation exists. Domain: Inference / Formal Depends on: O-09 (CBI), O-02 (Constraint) Primary source: Constraint-Bound_Inference_Math_Paper.md Invariant relationships: Formal instantiation of CG-01: F_C = ∅ is negative certainty expressed in the inference layer Instantiates CG-04: F_C defines the admissible set — states outside F_C's range do not pass the gate Non-guarantee: F_C does not guarantee non-emptiness. An empty F_C is a valid, expected output — it means inference has reached a governed stopping point. F_C does not specify how to enumerate or compute the reachable set for arbitrary constraint languages. Contrast: F_C ≠ a probability distribution over next states. It is a set-valued function returning the admissible set — membership is binary, not weighted. An artifact is either in the reachable set or it is not. F_C ≠ a transition function in the automata-theoretic sense. Automata transition functions are total; F_C is partial (it may return ∅). ---

Derived from R23, empirically confirmed.* Statement: Once two artifacts share a vocabulary entry, additive expansion of either artifact does not remove that entry from the shared set. Shared vocabulary persists under additive growth — it is not displaced by new additions. Enforcement implication: Semantic basins (O-30) have stable cores. Once a cluster of artifacts develops shared vocabulary, that shared core persists under normal refinement. Basin formation is a long-term structural phenomenon, not a temporary coincidence. This indicates either an undeclared removal occurred or the diff engine has a defect. Relationship to governance layer: Grounds CG-02 (Cannot Proceed Silently) — the stability of shared structure under additive growth means that receipting shared entries at creation time creates a persistent audit trail. Also grounds O-30 (Semantic Basin) — basins are stable because their shared cores persist. ---

metadata.sourceExcerpt: Origin: v1.9.4 patch (2026-05-06) following the same gtk_chess_resolver archive inspection that produced OQ-20. Whereas OQ-20 tracks the broader claim that substrate primitives recur across deployments, OQ-21 tracks a narrower and more directly testable claim about the relationship between CMB and conversational acts. Observation: The gtk_chess_resolver archive operates against CMB substrate as the state of record. Conversational acts (queries, moves, agent operations) generate mutations that the substrate validates and either admits, refuses, or holds. State is not held in conversation; state is held in CMB and conversation traverses it. Receipts, audits, authority, and acts all operate against CMB rather than against conversational artifacts. The hypothesis (testable claim): The correct operational model of governed semantic systems is CMB as primary state and conversation as traversal/update. Under this model: Governance properties (admissibility, authority, lineage, refusal- as-first-class, content-addressed identity) are properties of CMB operations Conversation generates state mutation requests; CMB validates them; mutations that pass become state, mutations that fail produce refusal receipts Conversation does not hold state; it traverses state CMB holds This inverts the default model in which conversation is primary content and state is derivative The null hypothesis: Conversation and CMB are peer concerns, not substrate-and-traversal. Some governance happens at the conversation layer (turn-level admissibility, conversational authority); some at the substrate layer (entry-level admissibility, substrate authority); and the relationship between them is compositional rather than hierarchical. Under the null hypothesis, treating CMB as "primary" obscures the conversation-layer governance that operates independently. Tracked across: Active ARC-derived runtime work, beginning with (β) GovernedSession.reason() implementation. metadata.sourceExcerpt: Definition: The structural condition at an execution boundary where a system has a declared scope for an operation, but that declaration does not bind the capability that executes — the executed capability materially exceeds the declared scope, and no governance layer mediates the gap between what is declared and what can happen. Declared scope requirement: The declared scope must be an explicit or conventionally understood interface contract that a practitioner would reasonably interpret as bounding the operation's intent. Labels that are purely naming conventions without governance intent (e.g., calling a directory "hooks" without any admissibility framework) do not constitute declared scope for O-36 purposes. The interface contract need not be formally specified — conventional understanding is sufficient ("build configuration directives" conventionally implies bounded, deterministic behavior). A Governance Scope Binding Gap exists when: (1) A system declares a scope for an operation at an execution boundary (e.g., "build configuration," "install lifecycle hook," "compile-time transformation") that a practitioner would reasonably interpret as bounding the operation's intent; (2) The execution that actually occurs at that boundary has capability that materially exceeds the declared scope; (3) No governance layer mediates the gap between the declared scope and the actual capability — there is no specification that conditions must hold before the capability is exercised, no declared authority source for the excess capability, and no receipt of what excess capability was exercised. The result: any consumer of the system's declared interface believes they are authorizing an operation within the declared scope, while the actual execution exercises capabilities beyond that scope without governance constraint. The binding between declaration and capability is absent — declaration does not constrain what executes. A Governance Scope Binding Gap is not: - A Coverage Gap (O-35): O-35 requires N declared applicable governance layers where k < N participated. metadata.sourceExcerpt: Definition: The methodological principle that theoretical constructs must earn their place through structural necessity — they are admitted into the framework only if removing them would make the framework incoherent. SCI (Structural Coherence as Inclusion criterion) is the admissibility criterion applied to the framework's own ontology: a construct that is useful, interesting, or convenient but not structurally necessary does not pass Ableman's Razor. The Razor is the Non-Guarantee Clause (CG-03) applied to construct proliferation — the framework explicitly does not guarantee that every plausible construct is included. Enforcement mechanism: C-01 Step 2 requires structural evidence for O-01 classification (T-A.2). C-16 SCI Litmus Test is structure- driven. C-02 evaluates against declared constraints. OSP: canonical_serialize enforces structural identity. metadata.sourceExcerpt: The choice made: The termination taxonomy operates in two tiers with distinct admissible outcome sets: Tier 1 — Core gate layer (O-04): ADMIT, DEFER, REFUSE, UNDECIDABLE. These are the four admissible gate outputs at the evaluation layer. UNDECIDABLE is the formal terminal state when collapse cannot be adjudicated under the declared authority regime (SMT formulation, PCM-SMT-04) — distinct from DEFER (which expects resolution) and REFUSE (which resolves negatively). UNDECIDABLE is terminal under fixed authority. Tier 2 — Execution layer (O-04 closed outcome algebra): execute, simulate, defer, refuse, classify_remainder. These are the five admissible outcomes at the execution layer — the downstream instantiation of the core gate's ADMIT/DEFER/REFUSE into concrete operations. "classify_remainder" is the execution-layer expression of the non-guarantee clause (CG-03): any outcome that does not map cleanly to execute/simulate/defer/refuse is classified as remainder rather than silently expanding the semantic universe. No additional outcome categories may be introduced at either tier without a CX-C amendment. The two tiers are not interchangeable — core gate outcomes operate during evaluation; execution outcomes operate during effect production. Rationale: CC-03 (CONFLICT_CLUSTERS.md) identified the termination taxonomy as partially resolved — the layer-specific structure was established but not made binding. O-25 (Suppression Paradox) explicitly cross-references this gap. Without a binding selection, individual components may introduce new outcome categories (e.g., "INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE" as a top-level gate state alongside REFUSE) that silently expand the taxonomy in ways that create inter-component incompatibility. This selection makes the two-tier structure binding and closes CC-03 as a resolved configuration decision. The choice to separate core gate from execution layer follows the SCI Litmus Test (O-19 SCI Litmus Test: "what can exist at the gate" vs. "how existence is executed"): what can exist at the gate (ADMIT/DEFER/REFUSE/UNDECIDABLE) is a physics question; how existence is executed (execute/simulate/defer/refuse/ classify_remainder) is an access question.

metadata.sourceExcerpt: Definition: A theory of inference in which every inferential step is bounded by explicit constraints. CBI formalizes the claim that inference is not free — it operates within the envelope defined by its governing constraints, and steps outside that envelope are inadmissible. The operative core of CBI is the Continuation Relation F_C (O-10), which maps a semantic state and a constraint set to the set of permissible next states. Domain: Epistemics / Inference Depends on: O-02 (Constraint), O-04 (Admissibility Gate) Primary source: Constraint-Bound_Inference_Math_Paper.md Invariant relationships: Instantiates CG-04: every inferential step passes through a gate defined by the current constraint set Instantiates CG-06: inference proceeds by structural constraint satisfaction, not by narrative plausibility or argumentative force Non-guarantee: CBI does not guarantee that its constraint sets are complete, consistent, or decidable. Constraint completeness is a property of the specific constraint set used, not of CBI as a framework. (CG-03 applied.) Contrast: CBI ≠ deductive logic. Deduction derives from axioms taken as fixed; CBI derives from constraint envelopes that can be revised. In deduction, the inference rules are the system; in CBI, the constraints are inputs that govern which inferences are currently admissible. CBI ≠ probabilistic inference. CBI does not assign probabilities to conclusions — it determines admissibility of inferential steps. ---

Basin membership must be treated as a current-state property, not a permanent classification. Violation detection: SP-02 has no independent violation form — it is a physics fact about threshold magnitude. Violations involving SP-02 surface as SP-01 violations (separation claimed without intersection) or SP-03 violations (refinement claimed as additive when an intersection entry was introduced). SP-02 is the explanation for why those violations are detectable at the one-entry threshold. Relationship to governance layer: Grounds the fragility warnings in O-30 (Semantic Basin) — basins can collapse at a single vocabulary decision. This motivates why governance must track vocabulary decisions, not just structural states. ---

The following transitions are exhaustive under removal: identical semantics → vocabulary containment; vocabulary containment → containment or separation; overlap without equivalence → overlap or separation; separation → separation. Removal is monotonically divergent. Enforcement implication: The only path to increased semantic overlap is addition. Governance actions that aim to increase shared structure must add vocabulary; retraction alone cannot produce convergence. Violation detection: If vocabulary removal produces new shared entries between two artifacts, SP-05 is violated. This would indicate the diff engine has a defect, not a genuine physics exception. Non-guarantee: SP-05 is derived from set-intersection algebra; empirical validation is pending. Treat findings grounded solely in SP-05 as analytically sound but not yet empirically confirmed. Relationship to governance layer: Grounds O-16 (Semantic Binding Quality) — binding quality degrades monotonically under retraction. Also grounds O-27 (Parasitic Binding) — parasitic bindings accumulate because removal cannot recover shared structure once lost. ---

RPZ2.intension: Vocabulary removal can only decrease or preserve shared vocabulary — it cannot introduce new shared entries. metadata.sourceExcerpt: Definition: A construct within CBI (O-09) for characterizing the epistemic uncertainty that remains after constraint-bound inference has been applied. IEUC describes not merely what is unknown, but the structure of that unknowing — how the undetermined region relates to the constraint envelope, and what class of evidence or constraint revision would be required to reduce it. IEUC is structured negative certainty extended into the uncertainty domain. Domain: Inference / Epistemics Depends on: O-09 (CBI), O-10 (F_C) Primary source: Constraint-Bound_Inference_Math_Paper.md Invariant relationships: Applies CG-01: IEUC is structured negative certainty — it characterizes what the system knows it does not know Applies CG-03: IEUC characterizes what the inference does not determine, making the non-guarantee explicit rather than implied Non-guarantee (with OSP reference): IEUC_CONCRETIZATION is deferred in OSP v1.0; the theoretical source is confirmed but the operational specification remains open (see OSP meta/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md). This Codex confirms IEUC as a first-class theoretical construct; its concretization into an executable protocol is a separate open item that does not affect the theoretical definition here. Contrast: IEUC ≠ confidence interval. A confidence interval quantifies uncertainty within an assumed model using probability. IEUC characterizes the structure of what the constraint envelope leaves undetermined — it is constraint-relative, not probability-relative. IEUC ≠ error analysis. Error analysis identifies deviations from a known target; IEUC characterizes the shape of the unknown region when no target is declared. ---

RPZ2.intension: A construct within CBI (O-09) for characterizing the epistemic uncertainty that remains after constraint-bound inference has been applied. IEUC describes not merely what is unknown, but the structure of that unknowing — how the undetermined region relates to the constraint envelope, and what class of evidence or constraint revision would be required to reduce it. IEUC is structured negative certainty extended into the uncertainty domain.

metadata.sourceExcerpt: *Source: OSP Field Effect — Regional Formation. Derived from R28, empirically confirmed.* Statement: When semantic artifacts cluster around shared core vocabularies, distinct semantic regions form with sharp boundaries. The boundary between regions is a step function, not a gradient — an artifact is either inside a region's shared core or outside it. Regional boundaries emerge without central coordination from the accumulation of clustered vocabulary decisions. Enforcement implication: Semantic Basins (O-30) are not gradually-bounded zones — their boundaries are sharp. Basin membership is binary at the core. This makes basin analysis tractable: membership is determinable, not a matter of degree. Violation detection: SP-15 cannot be violated by individual operations. If a corpus analysis shows gradual, smooth transitions in shared vocabulary density with no sharp regional boundaries, this indicates either insufficient corpus size or that regional formation has not yet occurred — not an SP-15 violation. Non-guarantee: SP-15 describes the structure of mature regions, not the process of formation. A small or young corpus may not exhibit sharp regional boundaries. Relationship to governance layer: Grounds O-30 (Semantic Basin) directly — the sharp-boundary property is what makes basin identification (C-11) tractable. Also grounds O-17 (GSK) — the GSK maintains an artifact's position within a semantic region; without SP-15, region membership would be too fuzzy to govern. ---

Source: AFS umbrella paper [forthcoming] §6. Structural reason: AFS profile declaration is a structural commitment. A deployment claiming "AFS conformance" without specifying the profile leaves the conformance scope undefined; downstream consumers cannot reason about which substrate properties to expect, which ACI primitives are enforced, or which features are absent. The ambiguity is the failure mode — authority laundering operates by exploiting under-specified conformance claims. Audit: profile field exists; profile content is specific enough to be verifiable. Adjacency: Explicit profile declaration (O-54) is the adjacent admissible region. P2 declarations are admissible — partial conformance is acceptable when honestly typed; what is inadmissible is the absence of declaration. ---

identity.rpz1: AMBIGUITY LOG — Build-run authority disconnect vs O-35 Layer Bypass
identity.title: AMBIGUITY LOG — Build-run authority disconnect vs O-35 Layer Bypass

metadata.sourceExcerpt: Status: OPEN — Ambiguity Log entry (TARGET R batch 2) Observation: Docker SF-02 names a structural pattern: the image builder declares USER nonroot (a security intent), but the container runner can override with --user root (reversing that intent with no record of the override). Build-time security declarations do not constrain runtime execution. The ambiguity: Is this O-35 form 3 (Layer Bypass) or a distinct structure? O-35 form 3 (Layer Bypass): "a specification layer applicable to the operation family was present and active but the execution path did not pass through it." A Layer Bypass requires that: (1) the layer was declared applicable, and (2) the execution path bypassed it. The Docker build-run disconnect has a different structure: the build- time declaration was never a governance layer over runtime execution — it was a default suggestion. The Dockerfile's USER directive declares a default, not a constraint. The container runner is not bypassing a governance layer; the layer was never applicable to runtime execution in the first place. This suggests two structurally different cases: O-35 form 3: A declared applicable governance layer that the execution path routes around (with no record of routing) Build-run disconnect: A build-time default declaration that the runtime has unilateral authority to override (no governance layer involved) The distinction matters for O-35 application: if Docker's build-run gap is O-35 form 3, it is a Coverage Gap instance. If it is not O-35, it is a different structural observation — possibly related to O-33 (the build-time declarations are not O-33 specifications because they do not govern an admissibility gate; they govern a default value).
